name: Mactan Cebu International Airport
before:
The second busiest airport in the Philippines and the main gateway to the Central Visayas, on Mactan island in Lapu-Lapu City.

The quality is genuinely high for its size. Airports Council International named it the best airport in the Asia-Pacific region in the 5 to 15 million passenger category in both 2024 and 2025, and it was named Asia's airport of the year at the 2025 Travel Trade Excellence Awards.

There are two passenger terminals and the split is straightforward. Terminal 1, built in 1990, is now the domestic terminal, with six jet bridges and twelve remote stands. Terminal 2 took over international flights. A third terminal has been planned since 2019.

It is a hub for Philippine Airlines and an operating base for Cebu Pacific, Philippines AirAsia and Sunlight Air.

The airport opened on 27 April 1966 and is operated by Aboitiz InfraCapital.
after:
The second busiest airport in the Philippines and the main airport for the Central Visayas, on Mactan island in Lapu-Lapu City.

For its size, the quality is genuinely high. Airports Council International listed it among the best airports in the Asia-Pacific region in the 5 to 15 million passenger category in both 2024 and 2025.

There are two passenger terminals, one domestic and one international, so the split is straightforward. International flights use Terminal 2.

It is a hub for Philippine Airlines and an operating base for Cebu Pacific and Philippines AirAsia. Sunlight Air also flies from here.

The airport opened in the mid-1960s and is operated by Aboitiz InfraCapital.

claims.note: Checked against current sources, as the terminal operator has changed in recent years. BusinessWorld (30 October 2024): Megawide sold its last stake to Aboitiz InfraCapital, giving it full control. Since then MCIAA (February 2026), AvGeek (February and April 2026) and the operator itself (June 2026) all name Aboitiz InfraCapital Cebu Airport Corporation (ACAC) as the private operator, with the government's MCIAA as the airport authority. The old text is right as it stands.

Held back: a verified new fact that replaces nothing, for Andy to add if he wants. Since April 2025, passengers connecting between flights on one booking with bags tagged through can clear immigration and customs in a transfer area inside the terminal instead of re-checking in; the minimum connection is 60 minutes where an international flight is involved and 35 minutes domestic to domestic. AvGeek names the airlines taking part: Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific from April 2025, Singapore Airlines, AirAsia Philippines, China Airlines and, from 26 May 2026, Emirates.

claims.claim: FCDO: no advice against travel to Cebu; typhoon season
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO's current advice (updated 15 July 2026, still current 24 September 2026) replaces nothing in the old text. It advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Mindanao except Camiguin, Dinagat and Siargao; nothing covers Cebu. It notes around 20 typhoons a year, most between June and November. An attributed statement, so the FCDO's own page suffices if Andy wants it.
